title: Change data capture (CDC): the database as a source of events

videos.script: Before PostgreSQL changes a single row, it writes down what it is about to do. That diary is the write-ahead log. {{wal}} It exists so the database survives a crash. And it holds something the tables never do: everything that happened, in the order it became true. {{history}} Ana opens a slot on that log, plays a day of trade, and reads it back. Two hundred and eleven transactions, each one whole, each one after it committed. {{slot}} She applies the customers' changes to a copy in the warehouse, night after night. {{apply}} On the fourteenth a customer is erased. The delete arrives like any other line, and the copy agrees with the shop, row for row. {{delete}} Then she looks at a second slot, one nobody ever read. It has kept every byte of the log since it was created. {{forgotten}} On a busy database, that is how change data capture fills a disk and stops the tills.
